blockingFindings.title: Canonical JSON parse failures use the wrong error code
blockingFindings.issue: parseJson() converts malformed canonical state, Spec, and catalog JSON into CANONICAL_RECORD_INCONSISTENT, but canonical parse failures must be reported as CANONICAL_RECORD_UNREADABLE.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Update parseJson() to emit CANONICAL_RECORD_UNREADABLE for JSON decoding failures while retaining CANONICAL_RECORD_INCONSISTENT for post-parse identity, schema, and integrity validation.
blockingFindings.rationale: R13 mandates UNREADABLE for canonical parse failures; the current implementation emits a contradictory public error code.

blockingFindings.title: Malformed Activity ledger JSON is classified as integrity failure
blockingFindings.issue: readConfirmedLedger() catches JSON.parse(line) failures together with schema and contiguous-order failures and always emits CANONICAL_RECORD_INCONSISTENT. A malformed ledger line is a canonical parse failure and must use CANONICAL_RECORD_UNREADABLE.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Separate JSON decoding from FlowActivity validation in readConfirmedLedger(): classify JSON.parse failures as CANONICAL_RECORD_UNREADABLE and retain CANONICAL_RECORD_INCONSISTENT for Activity schema, duplicate-ID, and confirmation-order violations.
blockingFindings.rationale: R13 explicitly separates parse/read failures from ledger integrity failures, so the broad catch produces the wrong externally observable error classification.

blockingFindings.title: Success consumer accepts null page limit
blockingFindings.issue: pageInfo() permits limit: null, and success() uses it for activities responses. R8 requires a successful activities pageInfo.limit to be an integer; null is valid only for known-resource errors.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Make pageInfo validation context-specific: require a bounded integer for success responses and allow null only in the error branch. Add a rejection assertion for a successful response with limit: null.
blockingFindings.rationale: The compatibility consumer accepts a response that violates the mandatory Schema Revision 1 activities success contract.

blockingFindings.title: Consumer hardcodes the page limit
blockingFindings.issue: pageInfo() compares limits against literal 100 instead of the centrally managed production resource limit, despite importing FLOW_QUERY_LIMITS.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Use the canonical page-limit field from FLOW_QUERY_LIMITS, adding or exporting it from the production contract if necessary, so consumer validation and request validation share one limit.
blockingFindings.rationale: The task implementation notes require resource limits to be shared directly from production; the literal can silently diverge from the public contract.

blockingFindings.title: Known error codes are not checked against their required paths
blockingFindings.issue: error() verifies that error.path is merely a string and that error.code is known, but it never enforces the required code-to-path mapping. For example, INVALID_JSON with /canonical would be accepted.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Reuse a centrally managed production error-contract mapping or validator in error(), and add a fixture assertion covering a known code with an incorrect path.
blockingFindings.rationale: R13 fixes the public path for every error code; accepting mismatched pairs means the consumer does not verify the required error contract.

blockingFindings.title: Symlinked canonical records use the wrong error code
blockingFindings.issue: readBoundedFile() opens records with O_NOFOLLOW, but an ELOOP failure is caught by the generic branch and converted to CANONICAL_RECORD_UNREADABLE. A symlinked canonical record is an identity/integrity violation and must be reported as CANONICAL_RECORD_INCONSISTENT.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Handle ELOOP in readBoundedFile() as identityCode before the generic read-error conversion, preserving CANONICAL_RECORD_INCONSISTENT for symlink identity failures.
blockingFindings.rationale: R13 requires identity and integrity failures to use CANONICAL_RECORD_INCONSISTENT; the current O_NOFOLLOW failure path emits the contradictory public error code.

blockingFindings.title: Invalid cursor errors expose selected Version metadata
blockingFindings.issue: runFlowQueryCli() includes selectedFlowVersion and availableFlowVersions for every QueryRequest error except SPEC_NOT_FOUND and FLOW_VERSION_NOT_FOUND. Therefore INVALID_CURSOR responses expose the discovered Version, contradicting the required null selection for invalid selection errors and the integration fixture expectation.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Handle INVALID_CURSOR like other pre-selection errors: emit selectedFlowVersion: null and availableFlowVersions: [] while retaining Version metadata for CURSOR_QUERY_MISMATCH after cursor binding has been validated.
blockingFindings.rationale: R12 requires selected Version metadata only when the requested Version is successfully established; the supplied integration test explicitly requires invalid cursor responses to omit both selection and available Versions.

blockingFindings.title: Symlinked canonical records use the wrong error code
blockingFindings.issue: readBoundedFile() opens records with O_NOFOLLOW, but ELOOP is converted by the generic catch branch into CANONICAL_RECORD_UNREADABLE. A symlinked canonical record is an identity/integrity violation.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Handle ELOOP in readBoundedFile() using identityCode so symlink identity failures emit CANONICAL_RECORD_INCONSISTENT.
blockingFindings.rationale: R13 requires identity and integrity failures to use CANONICAL_RECORD_INCONSISTENT; the current O_NOFOLLOW failure path emits the contradictory public code.

blockingFindings.title: Catalog verification scans an unbounded artifact tree
blockingFindings.issue: queryCatalogManagedFiles() recursively uses synchronous readdirSync/lstatSync without enforcing MAX_ARTIFACTS or another bounded entry count. A canonical Version containing many unmanaged entries can cause unbounded query work before the catalog limit is applied.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Bound the recursive catalog-managed entry count at MAX_ARTIFACTS plus one and raise CANONICAL_RECORD_INCONSISTENT immediately when exceeded, while preserving the existing catalog consistency check.
blockingFindings.rationale: R8 requires bounded canonical reading and count limits; the current verification path can traverse an arbitrarily large directory tree.

blockingFindings.title: Ledger-mismatch artifact validation bypasses bounded safe reads
blockingFindings.issue: In verifyQueryCatalog(), the ledger-digest-mismatch branch reads associated artifact content with fs.readFileSync(location.resolve(artifact.relativePath)). This bypasses O_NOFOLLOW, regular-real-file checks, and bounded read handling after the artifact has otherwise been verified.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Reuse a bounded, O_NOFOLLOW-protected read result for contentContract.assertCatalogAssociation(), or route this read through readBoundedFile() with the descriptor size and canonical error classification.
blockingFindings.rationale: R8 requires canonical reads to enforce safe file identity and byte bounds; this branch directly follows the internal path and performs an unbounded synchronous read.

blockingFindings.title: Consumer and CLI disagree at the response byte limit
blockingFindings.issue: runFlowQueryCli() checks MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES against the JSON payload before appending its newline, while consumeSerialized() checks the complete CLI serialization including that newline. A payload exactly at the shared limit is emitted successfully but rejected by the compatibility consumer.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Align the boundary definition in consumeSerialized() and runFlowQueryCli(); for example, validate the emitted JSON plus newline in the CLI and retain the same framing rule in the consumer, or explicitly exclude one terminal newline before the consumer limit check.
blockingFindings.rationale: R8 requires bounded activity responses and T-9 requires the consumer to share the centrally managed response limit. The current producer/consumer disagreement makes a valid boundary response fail compatibility validation.

blockingFindings.title: Catalog content read failures are misclassified
blockingFindings.issue: In verifyQueryCatalog(), the ledger-digest-mismatch branch uses readBoundedFile(), which throws QueryError with CANONICAL_RECORD_UNREADABLE for missing or permission-denied artifacts. readCatalog() then catches that error, isCanonicalReadError() does not recognize QueryError instances, and the failure is re-emitted as CANONICAL_RECORD_INCONSISTENT.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Preserve QueryError classification in readCatalog() or extend isCanonicalReadError() to recognize CANONICAL_RECORD_UNREADABLE QueryErrors before wrapping verification failures.
blockingFindings.rationale: R13 requires canonical parse/read/permission failures to emit CANONICAL_RECORD_UNREADABLE, while CANONICAL_RECORD_INCONSISTENT is reserved for identity and integrity failures.

blockingFindings.summary: Catalog content read failures are misclassified

blockingFindings.title: Artifact read failures are misclassified
blockingFindings.issue: Cataloged artifact read, permission, or missing-file failures can be returned as CANONICAL_RECORD_INCONSISTENT instead of CANONICAL_RECORD_UNREADABLE.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Preserve filesystem/read failures as CANONICAL_RECORD_UNREADABLE and reserve CANONICAL_RECORD_INCONSISTENT for integrity or schema violations.
blockingFindings.rationale: This unresolved R13 contradiction violates the canonical-record error contract.

blockingFindings.title: Artifact digest canonicalization loses an own __proto__ key
blockingFindings.issue: canonicalJson() does not faithfully serialize an object containing its own __proto__ property, so artifact digests can differ from the artifact bytes.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Serialize own keys, including an own __proto__ key, without prototype reinterpretation, and add a digest regression assertion.
blockingFindings.rationale: This unresolved R7 defect makes artifact integrity verification unfaithful.

blockingFindings.title: Historical replay skips activity and resulting-state integrity checks
blockingFindings.issue: Historical-state validation checks ordering and evidence but may bypass Activity node/transition validation and equality of replayed state with stored state.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Apply the same FlowActivity node, transition, and resulting-state checks to historical confirmation replay before accepting canonical state.
blockingFindings.rationale: This unresolved R8 gap can accept inconsistent canonical history.

blockingFindings.title: Metadata permits too many issues
blockingFindings.issue: The metadata projection accepts multiple issues although the public contract permits zero or one issue.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Enforce zero-or-one cardinality in the metadata projection and reject nonconforming canonical data.
blockingFindings.rationale: This unresolved R5 schema contradiction violates the public metadata contract.

blockingFindings.title: Metadata blocker fields are not derived consistently
blockingFindings.issue: Metadata does not fully enforce the blocked/blocker/nextAction relationship or blocker:null when unblocked.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Derive blocked, blocker, and nextAction using the documented precedence, emit blocker:null when unblocked, and reject missing blocker evidence as canonical inconsistency.
blockingFindings.rationale: This unresolved R5 violation produces inconsistent lifecycle and blocker metadata.

blockingFindings.title: Version discovery follows symlinkable directories
blockingFindings.issue: Path-based opendir during version discovery lacks O_NOFOLLOW, leaving a symlink TOCTOU risk while selecting canonical Flow versions.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Use no-follow descriptor-based directory traversal and reject symlink records before consuming discovered paths.
blockingFindings.rationale: This unresolved R8 filesystem-integrity risk can select data outside the canonical version directory.

blockingFindings.title: Errors expose an unestablished Flow Version
blockingFindings.issue: An error may report the requested Flow Version as selected before discovery and reader.open() establish that it exists and is valid.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Keep selected Flow Version null until canonical discovery and reader.open() succeed; clear selection and available-version fields for missing or identity-invalid versions.
blockingFindings.rationale: This unresolved R12 envelope defect misrepresents canonical resource identity.

blockingFindings.title: Metadata consumer does not verify the full public payload
blockingFindings.issue: The consumer only proves metadata consumption is non-null; it does not assert payload equality or usability of the required public fields without internal paths, raw catalogs, or generic envelopes.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Consume exactly one metadata item and compare the complete public metadata payload, including required fields, with the success fixture.
blockingFindings.rationale: This unresolved R4/T-9 acceptance gap does not establish the required metadata round-trip contract.

blockingFindings.title: Activity consumer lacks required success-shape scenarios
blockingFindings.issue: Consumer round-trip coverage omits bounded pages, cursor continuation, recordedAt filtering, and zero-match successful responses.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Add consumer assertions for bounded pagination, continuation cursors, inclusive/exclusive recordedAt filtering, zero-match success, pageInfo, items, and version fields.
blockingFindings.rationale: This unresolved R8/T-9 acceptance gap leaves required activity response branches unverified.

blockingFindings.title: Consumer rejects valid integer page limits
blockingFindings.issue: pageInfo(..., allowNullLimit=true) rejects integer limits even though activity error responses permit integer or null limits.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Allow a nonnegative integer limit in that assertion branch while retaining null acceptance where permitted.
blockingFindings.rationale: This unresolved R12/T-9 schema mismatch prevents consuming valid activity error responses.
